nodes.title: Note: MiniMax H3
widgets_values:
## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

## ComfyUI links
- [ComfyUI#15224](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15224)
- [🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

## About this workflow

This template runs the **reference-to-video (ref2va)** task using the `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` node. It takes any mix of reference images, videos, and standalone audio, and weaves them into the generation to lock in a character's identity, a style, a motion, a camera move, or a voice.

**Key inputs**

- **ref_images / ref_videos / ref_video_audios / ref_audios**: up to 9 reference images, 3 reference videos (each may carry its own paired soundtrack), and 3 standalone reference audio clips
- **prompt**: reference the inputs by tag, in the exact order they were connected, for example `<Picture 1>`, `<Video 1>`, `<Audio 1>`, then describe the target scene, motion, and audio
- **ref_image_size**: `match` scales references down to the generation's resolution (faster); `max` keeps up to a 2048px short edge for stronger identity fidelity, at the cost of speed since reference tokens ride along every sampling step
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector.
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node

**Sampling and decode**

- Sampler: `res_multistep`. `beta` or `normal` scheduler tends to outperform `simple` for reference-heavy prompts like this one
- The sampler's joint audio+video `LATENT` output feeds directly into both `VAEDecode` (video, `minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16`) and `VAEDecodeAudio` (audio, `minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32`); each decode node automatically pulls its own half out of the packed latent. `CreateVideo` then muxes the two into a single MP4 with synced sound
- The diffusion model here is `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors`, a different set of weights from the `fl2va` model used by the t2v/i2v templates

Ref2va's output is very sensitive to prompt wording; matching the reference tags precisely and being explicit about which reference drives which part of the shot tends to work best.

nodes.title: Input Text (Prompt)
widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the white space battleship in <Picture 1>: an extremely elongated anime-style capital ship whose lance-like prow extends forward as three long slender spikes, followed by a low panel-lined mid-hull with a deep recessed channel along its flank, a row of six pale-red dome-capped weapon pods mounted along the spine, a stepped upper superstructure carrying thin antenna masts, small sensor towers and a white radome sphere, two large swept dorsal fins with red-painted tips, a rounded forward command block with a horizontal red sensor slit, a large segmented cylindrical drum module at the stern quarter, small ventral fins and hull-side pods, and red hull numbering and small red unit markings printed on white armor. It is drawn as clean black line art with flat cel shading and light grey shadow planes.
<Subject 2> is the space environment in <Picture 2>: a large planet with a dark charcoal crust broken by branching networks of glowing orange-red magma cracks, an intensely bright red-white illuminated limb along its right edge, soft red nebula haze drifting in the surrounding blackness, and a dense field of small white stars.

summary:
[reference generation] The target video is a five-second single-shot space scene in which <Subject 1> cruises on a level course past <Subject 2>, framed in a three-quarter view from the front upper right. A slow tracking shot keeps the ship near the center of the frame while the planet drifts behind it, the ship banks slightly as red limb light sweeps across its hull, and the shot ends with the ship rimmed in red against the planet's glowing edge.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the triple-spike lance prow, the elongated hull proportions and dense panel lines, the row of six pale-red dome-capped weapon pods, the stepped superstructure with antenna masts and white radome, the red-tipped swept dorsal fins, the rounded command block with its red sensor slit, the segmented stern drum module, and the red numbering and markings on white armor are all retained; only space lighting, engine glow, and motion are newly added.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the dark crust with glowing branching magma cracks, the bright illuminated limb, the red nebula haze, and the dense starfield are retained as the background environment.

detailed_description:
The target video is 2D cel-animated anime mecha style with clean black line art, flat cel shading, and hard-surface mechanical-illustration detail, set in deep space.
[Shot 1] A wide three-quarter view from the front upper right frames <Subject 1>, the white space battleship, with its triple-spike lance prow reaching toward the lower left of the frame and the red-tipped dorsal fins, white radome, and segmented stern drum module rising toward the upper right. The panel-lined white hull, the row of six pale-red dome-capped pods along the spine, the thin antenna masts, the horizontal red sensor slit on the command block, and the red hull numbering all remain exactly as designed. Behind and below the ship, <Subject 2> fills the background: the dark crust webbed with glowing orange-red magma cracks, the bright red-white lit limb along the right side of the frame, red nebula haze, and small white stars. The camera holds a tracking shot at slow speed that keeps the hull near the center of the frame while the planet slides slowly to the left behind it, producing steady parallax between the ship and the burning crust. The ship advances prow-first on a level course and banks to starboard with small amplitude near the middle of the shot; as it rolls, hard red light from the planet's limb sweeps forward along the top of the fuselage, flares across the dorsal fins and the radome, and picks out the red markings, while the underside stays in cool grey shadow. Pale blue-white engine light pulses steadily behind the stern drum module and throws a soft glow onto its segmented rings. Short white puffs fire from maneuvering thrusters near the prow spikes, red navigation lights blink at the fin tips, and thin specular highlights travel backward along the six dome pods as the ship moves. Through the final seconds the camera pulls out with small amplitude at slow speed and tilts down slightly, so the ship grows smaller and more of the planet's curved disc enters the lower frame. On the last frame the ship crosses in front of the bright limb, its silhouette rimmed in red light with the engine glow still burning against the starfield.

overall_soundscape:
A deep sub-bass engine drone continues throughout the shot beneath a low metallic hull resonance. Short compressed hissing bursts mark the maneuvering thrusters, and faint intermittent electronic bridge pings pass underneath.

non_diegetic_music:
Sustained low brass at a slow tempo over a wide synth pad, joined midway by a slowly rising string figure that grows in volume and holds through the final frame.
